scope: Scenario expectations for the 15 tracked product domains. Runtime status is included only when the aggregate report or the scenario-specific sidecar has a matching source HEAD and current source hashes; it is not user acceptance or backend certification.

stateDefinitions.success: Successful response with populated data or receipt.
stateDefinitions.empty: Successful response with zero applicable records.
stateDefinitions.loading: Request remains in flight and the UI communicates that state.
stateDefinitions.error: Recoverable transport/server failure with a visible retry path.
stateDefinitions.pending: A contract-supported pending status or an in-flight mutation; keep these semantics distinct.
stateDefinitions.unknown: Transport response loss after a mutation; outcome remains unconfirmed until a read reconciliation.
stateDefinitions.duplicate: Repeated logical intent; no duplicate resource or balance effect, according to the operation contract.

limitations: Scenario definitions are not evidence that current mocks, pages or tests implement the expected state.
Direct shared-handler test references identify mapped test call sites, not response-branch coverage.
Unknown outcome is a client-observed transport ambiguity, not a value added to server status enums.
Backend owners must confirm idempotency and reconciliation semantics before any operation is certified.
Browser evidence is current when it has a recorded revision and every registered source-file hash still matches; unrelated commits alone do not make it stale.
Empty scenarios name only contract-applicable collection GET operations; reads outside each mapped empty state remain outside that scenario.
No user acceptance, staging or production evidence is claimed.

domains.surface: Admin dashboards, moderation and privileged controls

scenarios.expectedUi: Admin dashboards, moderation and privileged controls: A successful contract response renders the domain data and only actions allowed for the active persona.
Show an explicit no-results/no-activity state with the relevant filter or safe next action; preserve the distinction between no data and access denied.
Show an observable loading state; do not flash a false empty state or stale conflicting data.
Show a visible recoverable error and retry path; do not silently substitute fixtures or mutate the UI as if the request succeeded.
For a secured operation returning 401, clear/restore protected session state and route to authentication; do not expose stale protected data.
For a secured operation returning 403, show an explicit permission-denied state; do not present it as an empty successful result.
